    # preferring the nearest and longest plain string.
    candidates = []

            # Prefer cells above/left, but allow any text if needed.
            distance = abs(ans_row - cell.row) + abs(ans_col - cell.column)
            above_left_bonus = 0 if (cell.row <= ans_row and cell.column <= ans_col) else 1000
            candidates.append((above_left_bonus, distance, -len(val), cell))

    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("No source text string found in the workbook.")

    candidates.sort()
    src_cell = candidates[0][3]
    src = src_cell.value

    # Try to infer a grouping pattern from any existing example text in the workbook:
    # an example whose spaces removed equal the source string.
    inferred_group = None

        val = cell.value

        if isinstance(val, str) and not val.startswith("="):
            if val.replace(" ", "") == src and " " in val:
                parts = val.split(" ")
                lengths = [len(p) for p in parts if p != ""]
                if lengths:
                    # Use the most common leading group length.
                    inferred_group = lengths[0]
                    break

    # Try to infer group size from nearby formulas using MID/LEFT chunks if examples were absent.
    if inferred_group is None:
        formula_texts = []
        for cell in nonempty:

                formula_texts.append(val.upper())

        nums = []
        for f in formula_texts:

            for n in re.findall(r"MID\([^,]+,\s*\d+\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)", f):

        if nums:
            # Pick the most frequent positive chunk length.
